editorial:
Imagine falling in love at nine years old and having to fight the whole world just to stay with that person. You get to follow Werner, a shoemaker's son, and Felicitas, a girl from a wealthy family in 1890s Berlin. It starts out as a cute childhood crush, but as they grow up, the social gap between them becomes a huge wall. The vibe is very classic and romantic, focusing on how money and family status can tear two people apart. You will feel for Werner as he deals with a father-in-law who thinks he is not good enough for his daughter.

The acting is solid for its time, and the emotional build-up really works. While the pacing feels a bit slow compared to modern films, the drama keeps you interested in whether they will end up together. If you enjoy old-school romances, you should definitely track this down. Since it is an older gem, you might want to look for a high-quality restored version.
endingExplained: After years of being kept apart by class rules and the army, Werner and Felicitas finally find their way back to each other. The story wraps up by showing that true love is stronger than social status. Despite the efforts of Felicitas's father to keep them separate, the couple overcomes the obstacles. They eventually get to be together, proving that the bond they formed as children was meant to last a lifetime.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-fashioned love stories and historical dramas.
